_comment: SOURCE OF TRUTH for intended edits. EDIT-MANIFEST.md is rendered FROM this file. Anchors are re-resolved against the markdown on every run of tools/edit_manifest.py; a filed edit whose sentence has moved fails loudly rather than being patched from memory at implementation time.

edits.locus: `[^7]`, PDF p.660 — against the standing note at p.662
edits.rationale: `[^7]` asserts the Reformation argument as McGilchrist's flatly; the standing note two pages later says the summary was assembled from secondary accounts. `is his` and `assembled from secondary accounts` are different claims about the same sentences, and the STRONGER one is the one wired to the body. Three words move the honest version to the door where the reader actually knocks. The note already closes *See the standing note below.*, so no pointer is added — only the grade.
edits.anchor: metaphor removing the other mode's food — is his.
edits.replacement: metaphor removing the other mode's food — is his, reported here from secondary accounts.

edits.locus: PDF p.622 — against the standing note at p.626
edits.rationale: The chapter states Rule One (*say what the evidence carries, at the grade it carries it*) and demonstrates it on Jaynes — then exempts the one beat it is RESTING on. *it has been counted* is true and lets a reader take that the count is available and checked here; the chapter's own standing note says Snell is reported at second hand and his text is not in the repository. The replacement is still a sentence with no softener in it.
edits.anchor: It is countable, it has been counted, and anyone may recount it.
edits.replacement: It is countable, and Snell counted it — at second hand here, and checkable by anyone.
